items.title: Gulf oil exports plunge 49% as Hormuz bypass routes fall short

featured_image.name: Two pipelines helping Saudi Arabia, UAE bypass the Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
More than a month into the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the full scale of the disruption to global energy flows is becoming clear. Seaborne crude exports from Gulf states excluding Iran collapsed to 8.44 million barrels per day in March, a 49% drop from February's 16.58 million barrels, according to Arab economic reports cited by Calcalist. Despite weeks of logistical mobilization across the region, improvised bypass routes through Saudi pipelines, the UAE's Fujairah port, and Iraqi overland convoys have managed to replace only about half of normal export volumes.[1]

The disruption, triggered by Iran's effective blockade of the strait following the U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran that began on February 28, has reshaped the global oil market. S&P Global Ratings raised its 2026 oil price assumptions by $15 per barrel in March, to $80 for Brent and $75 for WTI, citing expectations of prolonged disruption. Energy prices have surged well above those forecasts, with Brent crude recently trading near the $109 range and analysts at Macquarie Group warning prices could reach $150 if the strait remains closed through April.[2][3][4]

items.title: Iran launches drone strikes on US bases in UAE, Kuwait

featured_image.name: Iran attacks cause fire in Kuwait, Bahrain; kill man in UAE - Al Jazeera

items.description: Iran's military launched a fresh wave of drone strikes against American military positions in the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait on Saturday, targeting radar systems and command infrastructure in what Tehran described as the second phase of its retaliatory operations against the US-Israeli alliance. The escalation came as the conflict, which began on February 28, entered its sixth week.

items.title: China, Russia call for ceasefire as Trump's Iran deadline nears

featured_image.name: Trump extends deadline for Iran to reopen oil route or face ... - PBS

items.description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said Sunday that achieving a ceasefire is the "fundamental way" to resolve the navigation crisis in the Strait of Hormuz, according to a Xinhua dispatch from Beijing. Wang made the remarks during a phone conversation with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov, as President Donald Trump's Monday deadline for Iran to reopen the strait draws near.[1]

items.title: Israel says Iran still holds 1,000-plus missiles five weeks into war

featured_image.name: Iran War

items.description:
More than five weeks into the war between Israel and Iran, Tehran's use of cluster munition-equipped ballistic missiles has emerged as one of the conflict's defining and most troubling tactics, scattering small explosive bomblets across Israeli population centers in attacks that bypass the country's layered air defense systems.

An Israeli Air Force intelligence officer publicly disclosed for the first time on April 4 that the military believes Iran still retains more than 1,000 ballistic missiles capable of reaching Israel. "The Iranians have more than 1,000 missiles that are capable of reaching Israel," Lt. Col. "Tet," who leads research on Iran's missiles and drones in the IAF's Air Intelligence Group, told Israel's Channel 12 news. At the war's outset, the IDF assessed Iran held approximately 2,500 ballistic missiles. Iran has since fired over 500 at Israel, launched hundreds more at Gulf states, and potentially lost hundreds in strikes on its launchers and depots.[1]

items.title: Container ship reports projectile splashes at UAE's Khor Fakkan port

featured_image.name: Container ship reports incident at UAEs Khor Fakkan port ...

items.description: The captain of a container ship reported witnessing multiple splashes from unknown projectiles in close proximity to the vessel at the United Arab Emirates' Khor Fakkan port on Sunday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said. Sharjah authorities confirmed they are actively dealing with the incident, and no injuries have been reported.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran hits Israel, Gulf energy sites in widening strikes

featured_image.name: Iran's use of cluster munitions against Israel may be a war crime

items.description: Iran launched multiple waves of ballistic missiles and drones on Sunday targeting Israel and Gulf states, striking the Neot Hovav industrial zone in southern Israel for the third time since the war began and damaging energy infrastructure in Kuwait, the UAE, and Bahrain.

items.title: Trump threatens Iran strikes after downed F-15 crew rescued

featured_image.name: Trump threatens Iran with "hell" if Hormuz strait isn't open in 48 hours

items.description: President Donald Trump announced early Sunday that a missing American crew member from an F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jet shot down over Iran had been rescued in what he called "one of the most daring Search and Rescue Operations in U.S. History," then escalated his rhetoric against Tehran with an expletive-laden ultimatum to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face devastating strikes on the country's infrastructure.

items.title: US-Israeli strikes expand to Iranian bridges, universities and hospitals

featured_image.name: Strikes On Iran Could Be War Crimes, Experts Warn—As Trump ...

items.description: The U.S.-Israeli war on Iran has entered a destructive new phase, with joint forces expanding their targeting beyond military sites to include universities, pharmaceutical factories, research institutions, petrochemical plants, and bridges, drawing sharp condemnation from international legal experts and threats of further retaliation from Tehran.

items.title: Iraqi oil tanker transits Hormuz after Iran exemption

featured_image.name: Iraqi crude tanker passes through Strait of Hormuz after Iran transit  exemption - The Economic Times

items.description: Iran announced on Saturday that Iraq would be exempt from all restrictions on maritime transit through the Strait of Hormuz, a move that could partially reopen the flow of Iraqi crude oil after more than five weeks of near-total shutdown at the world's most critical energy chokepoint.

items.title: Iranian missiles hit Negev chemical complex for third time

featured_image.name: Iran strike hits industrial zone in southern Israel

items.description: Iran launched multiple waves of ballistic missiles at Israel on Saturday and into Sunday, striking the Neot Hovav industrial zone south of Beersheba and scattering cluster munitions across central Israel in an escalation of the six-week-old conflict. The attacks wounded at least six people and caused widespread damage to residential buildings and infrastructure across several cities.

items.title: Israeli strikes kill 54 in Lebanon in 24 hours as Tyre evacuation ordered

featured_image.name: Israeli strikes pound Lebanese southern coastal city of Tyre

items.description:
Israeli airstrikes and drone attacks across southern Lebanon killed at least 14 people and wounded more than 25 others on Saturday, as warplanes carried out heavy strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs and the coastal city of Tyre, according to Lebanon's National News Agency.[1]

The attacks marked another deadly day in the escalating conflict between Israel and Hezbollah, now in its second month. Lebanon's Public Health Emergency Operations Center reported that the cumulative death toll since fighting resumed on March 2 has reached 1,422, with 4,294 wounded, including 126 children and 93 women.[2][3][4]

items.title: Trump aides push legal case for striking Iran's civilian infrastructure

featured_image.name: Testimony raises questions about Pete Hegseth's handling of secrets and  sensitive communications

items.description: Senior White House advisors have privately argued to President Trump that Iran's power plants and bridges are legitimate military targets, laying the legal groundwork for an escalation that military lawyers warn could violate international humanitarian law.

items.title: Nepal shifts to two-day weekend as energy crisis grips Asia

featured_image.name: Energy crunch amid West Asia conflict forces Bangladesh Govt to ...

items.description: From shortened workdays in Dhaka to dimmed billboards in Seoul, governments across Asia, Europe, and Africa are rolling out emergency austerity measures as the global energy crisis triggered by the Iran war's disruption of oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz intensifies.

items.title: Ex-IAEA chief urges Gulf nations to stop Trump's Iran war

featured_image.name: Trump issues 48-hour Hormuz Strait ultimatum, threatens Iran's ...

items.description:
Mohamed ElBaradei, the Nobel Peace Prize laureate and former head of the International Atomic Energy Agency, issued an urgent appeal on Saturday calling on Gulf nations and the United Nations to intervene against the U.S. military campaign in Iran, warning that President Donald Trump risks turning the Middle East into "a ball of fire."[1][2]

In a post written in Arabic on X, the 83-year-old former Egyptian diplomat wrote, "Please, once again, do everything in your power before this madman turns the region into a ball of fire." In a separate English-language post addressed to the United Nations, he asked: "Is there nothing that can be done to stop this madness?"[2][3]

items.title: Zelenskyy says Russia gave Iran intel on 50 Israeli energy sites

featured_image.name: Zelensky Says 'Regimes in Russia and Iran Are Brothers in Hatred' and Urges  Allies to Unite

items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of providing Iran with satellite intelligence on 50 to 53 civilian Israeli energy facilities, saying the data has helped Tehran carry out strikes on Israel's infrastructure. Zelenskyy made the claims in an interview with the Associated Press conducted on Saturday, sharing excerpts on his Telegram channel on April 5.[1][2]

items.title: Israeli airstrikes reach Beirut hospital area as Lebanon offensive escalates

featured_image.name: Lebanon says 13 killed in Israeli strike near Beirut hospital

items.description: Israeli airstrikes across Lebanon over the weekend killed civilians including two young girls and brought destruction close to the country's largest public hospital, as the military escalated its month-old offensive against Hezbollah.

items.title: J.P. Morgan warns oil stockpiles could hit crisis levels by May

featured_image.name: How to weather the global energy crisis: IEA - CNBC

items.description:
Crude oil prices exploded higher last week as the U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran entered its sixth week with no end in sight, sending shockwaves through global energy markets already reeling from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. WTI crude futures surged more than 11% on Thursday alone to close above $112 per barrel — their highest level since June 2022 — after President Donald Trump's national address failed to offer a timeline for ending the conflict or reopening the strait. Brent crude ended Thursday at $109.03, marking its seventh consecutive weekly gain.[1][2][3]

The rally was ignited by Trump's Wednesday evening address, in which he said Iran had been "decimated both militarily and economically" but warned of intensified U.S. military action ahead. He offered no path to reopening the Strait of Hormuz, instead declaring that "the countries of the world that do receive oil through the Hormuz Strait must take care of that passage". Markets interpreted the remarks as a signal that the conflict — dubbed Operation Epic Fury when it began on February 28 — could drag on for weeks longer.[2][4][1]

items.title: Zelenskyy makes first visit to Syria for defense talks

featured_image.name: Zelenskyy: Another four Middle Eastern countries request defence ...

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrived in Syria on Sunday for his first-ever visit to the country, meeting with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa to discuss defence cooperation amid the escalating regional conflict, according to two Syrian sources, including a government adviser.

The visit comes as Zelenskyy continues a broader push to deepen military ties across the Middle East, building on a whirlwind Gulf tour in late March and a stop in Istanbul on Saturday, where he held security talks with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.[1][2]

items.title: Artemis II enters lunar gravity ahead of Monday flyby

featured_image.name: NASA Answers Your Most Pressing Artemis II Questions

items.description:
Four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft are now deep in lunar space, closing in on the moon ahead of a flyby set for Monday, April 6 — the first time humans have ventured this far from Earth since the Apollo era more than five decades ago.

The Artemis II mission lifted off from Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Wednesday, April 1, carrying NASA astronauts Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, and Mission Specialist Christina Koch, along with Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen. By Sunday, the spacecraft had crossed into the lunar sphere of influence, where the moon's gravity exerts more force on Orion than Earth's does.[1][2]

items.title: Trump vows to hit Iran's power plants, bridges Tuesday

featured_image.name:
US–Israel war on Iran, day 36:
Trump gives Iran 48 hours to open Strait of Hormuz as US hunts for airman

items.description: President Trump dramatically raised the stakes in the five-week-old war with Iran over the weekend, first warning Saturday that Tehran has 48 hours to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face devastating consequences, then following up Easter Sunday morning with a profanity-laced post threatening to destroy the country's power plants and bridges starting Tuesday.
